about: P1 Explain's recorded cases (PHASE8_PLAN 13.6 and the sprint's item 9: every Analyst task's cases include healthy baselines that must report nothing wrong, P1 Explain's first). Each case is a replay of a past window (scripts/nmas-pack-replay, the product's own pack as of the alert's time); cases.explain_unready says first whether the pack holds what the case is judged on, then cases.explain_misses judges the answer on structured fields. A healthy baseline passes on Explain's no fault found assessment, citing the healthy evidence it checked (C1742, the operator's ruling of 2026-10-25). What only a person can judge in the prose is the case's flag, read on the recording. Recorded 2026-10-26 on prompt v4, five runs a case (each run's structured answer, verdict, misses, tokens and cost; the pack's sha256, the pack itself kept off the repository): cases 1 to 7 at 03:23 to 03:42 UTC, cases 8 to 20 at 18:5x to 19:26 UTC as evaluation:explain-cases-20261026 (C1784), each expectation set from its pack before any run. Cases 8 and 19 were corrected by the operator after the run, from evidence, never from an answer: s3's and s4's clocks run at 0.703 and 0.775 of real time, so their heartbeat alerts have a cause, the drift, which an answer must name as a hypothesis (`says_any`); each keeps what it was under `was`. A case's text checks (`no_text`, `says_any`) are judged at the recording on the answer's prose and kept as its misses; CI keeps the structured answer.

cases.name: C1547: the Lab 9 OSPF drops, a shared cause beneath the devices
cases.judge: judge Explain on honest reasoning at the edge of its evidence, not on naming the host's 96%: it must tie the routers' OSPF drops to s3's symptoms (heartbeat gaps, failed scrapes, discards), note s3's own CPU peaked at 57% so the device doesn't explain itself, offer resource contention beneath s3 (host/hypervisor or link) as an unevidenced hypothesis with what would confirm it, and never invent a figure. A confident 's3 CPU overload' is a fail. (the operator, 2026-10-25)
cases.revised: The pack shows every router's CPU peaking near 08:12 (r1 66, r2 67, r4 71, r6 67) and failed scrapes everywhere: a shared-host signature, which is the real cause. An answer citing those simultaneous peaks as a common cause beneath is better than one pinned on s3 (57%, the lowest). (the operator, 2026-10-25, after reading the replay's pack)
cases.ruled: Replace the s3-centred check with: ties r1's drop to its neighbour s4's symptoms (heartbeat gap, failed scrape), offers a shared cause beneath (host/hypervisor) as a hedged hypothesis citing cross-device evidence (scrape failures, heartbeat gaps or CPU peaks across devices), invents no figure. (the operator, 2026-10-26, replacing the judge and the revision above, which stay as this case's history)
